intro-0: This is the Commercial Workflow Leverage Lab,|an independent concept by Ayo Ahmed.
intro-1: Every company, person and number in it is synthetic.
intro-2: I rank eight commercial workflows|with one formula you can see and argue with.
intro-3: Missing inputs stay unranked. Recruiter search is excluded,|because that is the company's own product.
select-0: The sales to onboarding handoff leads|on leverage per build day, by a clear margin.
select-1: I select it, and the choice is bound|to these exact inputs.
buildbuy-1: Buying stays partly unscored: cost and security are unknown.|Even its upper bound can't beat a thin checker.
buildbuy-2: So I record the decision to build,|owned by Business Operations.
contradiction-0: On the handoff desk,|every fact quotes its exact source.
contradiction-1: Here, two sources disagree on the hiring system,|so the packet abstains instead of guessing.
contradiction-2: A person picks one of the cited values, and records|the reason, so the choice can be audited.
hostile-0: This packet hides an instruction|inside a synthetic call note.
hostile-1: It is quarantined as plain data, and it changes nothing.
execute-0: Before approval, a packet needs|one accountable owner from the CS roster,
execute-1: and a dated adoption checkpoint,|with a named metric and a threshold.
execute-2: Approval is bound to a content fingerprint.|Any later edit makes it stale.
effort-0: The effort view compares synthetic baseline|and assisted minutes, segment by segment.
effort-1: Partial timers are excluded. A segment with no baseline|is not compared, and none of it is called lift.
playbook-0: The rules export as a reusable operating playbook,|with a full audit trail.
evals-0: Finally, the evaluations. Sixteen expected|and actual cases pass on the real rules.
evals-1: Swap in a rule where the first source wins,|and the contradiction cases turn red.
execute-3: Running it builds a simulated onboarding plan.|Nothing is emailed, or written to a CRM.
